newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo appoints genetics head - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo appoints genetics head - WSJ.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc has named Dr. Allen Roses, a research neurologist who discovered a radical theory behind Alzheimer's disease, to head its new genetics department, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said Roses will run the company's new "genetics directorate," a research division that will seek to uncover the role human genes play in making some people especially susceptible to common diseases.

Roses, a research neurologist at Duke University Medical School in North Carolina, is expected to help Glaxo as it seeks improved medicines against asthma, arthritis, heart disease, diabetes, cancer and other illnesses.
In 1993, he proposed a controversial theory that people who inherit a particular version of a certain gene are at a high risk of developing Alzheimer's disease, a degenerative brain illness.
